title: ProxiML: Building Machine Learning Classifiers for Photonic Quantum Computing
problem: Quantum machine learning classifiers have not been systematically explored on photonic quantum computing platforms. The technical challenge is designing an ML classifier that can handle photonic hardware-specific noise while maintaining classification accuracy.
motivation: Quantum machine learning shows promise for improving productivity in ML classification, and photonic quantum platforms represent an unexplored but potentially advantageous hardware substrate.
method: ProxiML incorporates multiple noise-aware design elements for robust training and inference on photonic quantum devices. The classifier is evaluated on Xanadu's X8 photonic quantum machine using quantum circuits optimized for photonic hardware characteristics.
key_novelty: First systematic exploration of quantum ML classifiers specifically designed for photonic quantum platforms with integrated noise mitigation techniques.
contributions: Novel quantum ML classifier architecture (ProxiML) for photonic quantum devices
Noise-aware design elements enabling robust training and inference
Demonstration of >90% accuracy on 4-class classification tasks on real photonic hardware
Validation showing competitive performance with quantum ML on other quantum platforms
primary_theme: Quantum machine learning on photonic platforms
